newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Report critical of Apple Fields.
newsitem.headline: Report critical of Apple Fields.

text.p: Apple Fields has not provided enough information to its shareholders for them to make an informed decision on its proposed change of business direction, according to an independent report by accountants Arthur Andersen released on Tuesday.
Former Apple Fields' partnership investor Alan Galbraith commissioned the report to assist with an assessment of the material to be put to the company's shareholders' meeting on Thursday.
Apple Fields is proposing a change in direction to property ownership and development from orchard ownership.

"The report notes that the new property direction will require considerable cash resources to implement and there is no mention of where this cash will come from," Galbraith told journalists at a briefing in Wellington.
"The notice of meeting provides no detailed forecasts, but instead contains broad estimates."
Galbraith said the risks identified in the report include:
* uncertainty relating to the re-zoning process
* the risks of residential property cyclical trends
* the risks of the impact on the residential property market of approximately 2000 sections becoming available.
Galbraith said the report showed Apple Fields urgently needed either a significant asset disposition, rollover or replacement of existing debt facilities, or some othe form of capital injection.
"Apple Fields is currently dominated by two major assets, its real estate holdings and its shares in Dairy Brands Ltd," Galbraith said.
"Both of these assets provide limited income streams which seem unlikely to be sufficient to meet current cashflow requirements, including scheduled debt repayments."
Galbraith said Apple Fields had consistently maintained losses incurred by the company were due to the single desk selling policy of the New Zealand Apple and Pear Marketing Board.
"However, it is Arthur Andersen's conclusion that Apple Fields has failed to demonstrate conclusively that this policy is the major cause of the company's lack of financial success," he said.
Galbraith said he was not warning people against investing in Apple Fields, he was simply concerned potential investors had all the relevant information.
